Share SAML/SSO integration guide and metadata
Schedule detailed private deployment deep-dive with SE team

summary: Initial security posture discovery for Kepler Finance evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SOC 2/ISO status, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC model, audit logs & retention, encryption/KMS options, data residency and retention. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private for regulated data; next steps include sharing artifacts and scheduling a technical deep-dive.
transcript:
Header: 2026-06-24 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~44 minutes | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Maya (CISO, Kepler), Dean (Head of Platform, Kepler), Lina (SRE, Kepler)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan Lee from Redwood — AE. With me is Samir Patel, our systems SE.
[00:08] Samir: Hi folks. Quick agenda — high level security posture, compliance artifacts, SSO/SAML, encryption/KMS, audit logs and retention, and then next steps.
[00:18] Maya: Great, thanks. We're mainly trying to understand whether Redwood Hosted is acceptable or if we need Dedicated/Private for regulatory reasons. We have PCI-adjacent workflows and need strict retention and SSO.
[00:28] Dean: Also curious about per-token logging and whether we can turn off any PII capture.
[00:32] Jordan: Totally, that makes sense. To kick off — Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, we can share the artifacts under an NDA. For Dedicated we offer additional network isolation, and Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[00:48] Maya: When you say artifacts, is that the full audit or just a summary? We need the actual report excerpts to feed our audit team.
[00:54] Jordan: We can share SOC2 bridge letter and the ISO cert plus the SOC 2 report redacted per our legal. I'll send those PDFs after the call.
[00:59] Dean: What's the timeline for Private deployment? If we go Private, do we push into our VPC or do you host a control plane?
[01:06] Samir: For Private we give an option — customer-managed control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package for air-gapped setups. Usually planning is 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and your infra readiness. That includes KMS/HSM integration for key rotation.
[01:23] Lina: On KMS — do you support AWS KMS and external HSMs? Our keys must be customer-owned.
[01:29] Samir: Yes, we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and external HSM via KMIP. For Hosted we do envelope encryption with customer KMS keys when requested; for Dedicated and Private you can bring keys entirely within your KMS.
[01:42] Maya: Good. About SSO — we use SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. Do you support SCIM?
[01:49] Jordan: We do SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning in the Console. Samir, do you want to add notes on RBAC?
[01:55] Samir: Sure. We have role-based access in the Console with predefined roles and custom roles via fine-grained permissions. RBAC maps to your identity provider assertions. There are some limits today on nested groups — it's on the roadmap but for most enterprise setups we do group-to-role mapping.
[02:12] Dean: Are audit logs immutable? We need tamper-evidence and export to our SIEM.
[02:17] Samir: Audit logs are append-only and we provide streaming to S3 or to your SIEM via syslog / forwarder. For Private you can host the log endpoint entirely in your network. They are signed and include request id, user id, route, model version, and token counts.
[02:32] Maya: Token counts — is the request payload logged? We have to avoid logging sensitive input.
[02:36] Jordan: By default we retain minimal metadata and redaction can be applied. There's a knob to disable full-text request logging; then only metadata, request id, model id are recorded. For Hosted we recommend prefix caching instead of logging sensitive full inputs.
[02:52] Lina: Is there a data retention policy configurable per customer?
[02:56] Samir: Yes — retention windows are configurable. Hosted has defaults (30/90/365 days), Dedicated supports custom retention policies, and Private you control retention entirely.
[03:08] Dean: Encryption at rest — AES-256? In transit — TLS? We need FIPS-validated modules for some workloads.
[03:15] Samir: At rest we use AES-256-GCM. In transit is TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 by default). For FIPS we have a FIPS-compatible stack available for Dedicated/Private with HSM-backed keys. We can include FIPS attestations in the artifact bundle if needed.
[03:30] Maya: Ok. On the compliance side, do you provide per-customer tenancy or multi-tenant? For PCI-adjacent we require stronger isolation.
[03:38] Jordan: Dedicated gives you isolated GPU pools with tenant isolation; Private is single-tenant. Hosted is multi-tenant but logically separated. Many customers start on Hosted and then migrate to Dedicated once they hit retention or SLA requirements.
[03:52] Dean: About model variants — if you fallback to a cheaper model, is that logged? We need to know which model served a request.
[03:58] Samir: Yes, model version and actual deployed kernel are logged in the audit trail. We also provide a per-route cost and latency breakdown in the Console.
[04:07] Maya: Networking — can we restrict egress for Hosted? We need to ensure no outbound to unknown IPs.
[04:12] Samir: Hosted runs in our network and outbound is restricted, but if you need strict egress control, Dedicated/Private lets you define egress policies in your VPC and firewall.
[04:24] Lina: What about data residency — are you in EU, US regions? We have EU customer data residency requirements.
[04:30] Jordan: We have hosted regions in NA and EU and are expanding APAC. For strict residency we recommend Dedicated in the target region or Private in your region.
[04:38] Maya: Can you walk me through the SAML flow quickly — assertion, mapping to roles, and session length?
[04:44] Samir: Sure — after IdP SAML assertion, we validate signature, extract attributes (email, groups), map to RBAC roles. Sessions default to 1 hour with refreshable tokens; you can reduce that. We also support short-lived service tokens for automation.
[04:59] Dean: Does SCIM sync support deprovisioning immediately? We need accounts removed within the day for security.
[05:04] Jordan: SCIM supports immediate deprovisioning; in practice it depends on polling windows but we support push notifications for near-immediate revoke.
[05:14] Maya: About audit exports — how long do you keep logs natively? If we want 7 years, can you ship exports to our cold storage?
[05:20] Samir: Native retention is configurable; for long-term you can export to S3 Glacier or your archival store. We'll set up a lifecycle policy to push to Glacier after X days.
[05:31] Dean: There's also the question of model KV cache — any chance that keys or prefixes leak into logs?
[05:36] Samir: KV cache metadata can be logged but payload is not. We recommend disabling capture of any KV payloads. There's a setting per-deployment to avoid prefix caching that stores sensitive context.
[05:49] Lina: For the Dedicated environment, do you provide access to the underlying nodes for incident response?
[05:53] Samir: Not direct SSH into managed nodes, but we provide diagnostic bundles and secure remote debugging sessions with our ops team under NDA. For Private on-prem you have full access.
[06:05] Maya: Can you share an example audit record? Even a redacted snippet would help our risk team.
[06:10] Jordan: Yes, I'll attach a redacted example in the follow-up email.
[06:14] Dean: Ok, procurement question — what does the contract look like for Dedicated? Are there SLAs for latency?
[06:19] Jordan: Yes, Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. We'll provide specifics in the commercial pack. Pricing depends on reserved GPU hours and burst capacity.
[06:27] Maya: On encryption key rotation — do you rotate keys automatically or do we manage rotation windows?
[06:32] Samir: We support both. For Hosted you can opt into automatic rotation with customer-managed KMS; for Dedicated/Private you can control rotation schedules and bring your own rotation automation.
[06:42] Lina: Any penetration testing reports? We need recent pen test summaries.
[06:46] Jordan: We have a yearly external pentest; I will include the executive summary. Full reports under NDA.
[06:53] Maya: One more — are there any known gaps in SOC2 scope? For example backups, third-party subprocessors?
[06:59] Jordan: Subprocessors are listed in the artifact bundle. Backups are included in scope; we can provide control mappings to your requirements. If you want, Samir can map controls to Kepler's control list offline.
[07:09] Samir: Yep, we can run a control mapping (SOC2 control -> Redwood control) and return a table.
[07:13] Dean: That would be useful. Also, Lina — can you send us the specific retention & redaction policy you need?
[07:18] Lina: I'll draft and send by Tuesday.
[07:21] Jordan: Great. Any blockers on your side for starting a pilot?
[07:24] Maya: Procurement needs pricing and the SOC artifacts. Also we need to confirm SSO works with our Okta instance.
[07:30] Jordan: Ok we'll deliver artifacts and a SAML config guide. Samir, can we provision a sandbox Dedicated for a short pilot?
[07:36] Samir: Yes, we can spin up a sandbox Dedicated for testing — usually 2–4 dedicated accel nodes for a 2-week pilot. We'll scope latency/burst in the pilot.
[07:44] Dean: For the pilot do you need any network peering or just test keys?
[07:49] Samir: Depends — for basic tests just API keys and SAML. For latency testing we'll want a private peering or VPC endpoint to remove internet variance.
[07:58] Maya: If we go forward, is there a straightforward migration path from Hosted to Dedicated?
[08:03] Jordan: Yes, we support model pinning and route-level rollout. Migration is mostly config and capacity reservation, and we can help with truncation of logs and migration of retention policies.
[08:12] Dean: Any limitations on RBAC mapping for SCIM groups? Earlier you said nested groups are limited. How big a blocker is that?
[08:19] Samir: For most customers we map top-level groups to roles; nested groups may require a custom attribute mapping. We have a quick workaround using group attribute flattening in Okta.
[08:29] Lina: Ok.
[08:30] Jordan: Quick recap of next steps: I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts and pentest summary; Samir will send SAML/SCIM template and sample metadata; we'll provision a sandbox Dedicated pilot and schedule a technical deep-dive next week.
[08:46] Maya: Sounds good. Thanks, everyone.
[08:50] Jordan: Thanks all — we'll follow up with the bundle and the pilot proposal.
[08:54] (call ends)

Notes on quality: Minor transcription errors observed — 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'KV cash' in the automated notes, and 'Redwood Dedicated' appeared as 'Redwood Dedicate' once. There was occasional crosstalk.
